title: Contraction of log towers and descent of strict etale comparisons
statement:
Let $f:(Y,N)\to(X,M)$ be a strict etale morphism between locally Noetherian fs log schemes [def-trf-fs-log-blowup, lem-trf-log-fan-chart-blowup, def-weil-etale-morphism], with no surjectivity hypothesis on $f$. Let $B$ be a finite saturated log blowup tower over $X$ with nonempty coherent ordered centers, and let $D=f^*B$ be its recursive uncontracted pullback. Write $C(D)$ for the tower obtained by deleting exactly its whole-monoid centers [def-trf-strict-etale-log-blowup-procedure]. Let $v:W\to Y$ be a surjective strict etale cover. At every level the corresponding map from the uncontracted pullback of $D$ to $D$ is a scheme-theoretic base change of $v$; a center of $D$ is whole if and only if its restriction there is whole. There is a canonical ordered center-preserving isomorphism
$$v^*C(D)\simeq C(v^*D).$$
The retained ordered index set on both sides consists of exactly the same indices of $D$, including when several consecutive indices are deleted. The identifications across deleted levels are the canonical identity log morphisms, and the later centers are carried by these identifications to their original pulled-back ideals; proper principal centers are retained.

If $A$ is a contracted finite saturated log blowup tower over $Y$ and $C(v^*D)\simeq v^*A$ is an ordered center-preserving isomorphism over $W$, then there is a unique such isomorphism $C(D)\simeq A$ inducing it. Equivalently, the local contracted pullback comparison from $B$ to $A$ descends uniquely. Identity and composition equalities for these comparisons can be tested after a surjective strict etale cover of their source, using the induced covers at the intermediate tower levels. This includes their retained index maps and their actual log morphisms, so applies to consecutive strict etale morphisms and to towers of length zero.

proof.text: Write $D=(Y_n\to\cdots\to Y_0=Y)$, with center $J_i\subset N_i$ at stage $i<n$, and $E=v^*D$, with levels $W_i$ and centers $K_i$. Apply the first paragraph of [lem-trf-log-tower-cover-synchronization] to $D$ over $Y$ and $v$. It gives $W_i=W\times_Y Y_i$, with surjective strict etale projection to $Y_i$, and $K_i=N_{W_i}$ if and only if $J_i=N_i$. Its hypotheses hold because $D$ is the stipulated finite saturated tower, all centers are nonempty coherent, and $v$ is surjective strict etale. This application is entirely over $Y$ and assumes no surjectivity of $f$.

source.place: VIII 3.3.8--3.3.11 and proof of 3.3.15, pp.108--110: contracted pullbacks and testing equality after descent; non-surjective compatibility expanded.

proof.text: Let $S=\{i<n:J_i\ne N_i\}$, in its original order, and $r(i)=\#\{j<i:j\in S\}$ for $0\le i\le n$. By step 1 this same subset and count apply to $E$. Construct the identifications between level $i$ and contracted level $r(i)$ inductively. At $i=0$ use the identity. If $i\in S$, retain its blowup and its actual center and advance to level $r(i)+1$. If $i\notin S$, its blowup is canonically the identity by [lem-trf-log-tower-cover-synchronization]; compose the preceding identification with that identity and leave $r(i+1)=r(i)$. In this deletion case, a later ideal is carried along the inverse of this specified log isomorphism, rather than replaced by another ideal with isomorphic blowup. Thus any run of consecutive deletions uses a composite of these canonical identities. This is exactly contraction as defined in [def-trf-strict-etale-log-blowup-procedure]. No test for principality or for an isomorphic blowup is used, so proper principal centers remain.

source.place: VIII 3.3.8--3.3.11 and proof of 3.3.15, pp.108--110: contracted pullbacks and testing equality after descent; non-surjective compatibility expanded.

proof.text: Repeat this induction after pulling back to $W$. A retained stage in the contracted tower has the same base-changed blowup and pulled-back ideal as the corresponding retained stage of $E$: recursive pullback is defined by blowing up precisely that pulled-back ideal [def-trf-strict-etale-log-blowup-procedure]. Their unique isomorphism over the preceding level is supplied by the universal property of the saturated log blowup [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]: each of the two universal objects factors uniquely through the other, and the composites are identities by uniqueness. At a deleted stage both paths use the identity of step 2. Starting with the identity on $W$, induction therefore gives $v^*C(D)\simeq C(E)$, preserving every retained center and arrow. Both retained embeddings are the increasing enumeration of $S$; there is no shift ambiguity after successive deletions.

source.place: VIII 3.3.8--3.3.11 and proof of 3.3.15, pp.108--110: contracted pullbacks and testing equality after descent; non-surjective compatibility expanded.

proof.text: Now let $\alpha:C(E)\simeq v^*A$ be the given isomorphism. Compose it with step 3 to obtain an ordered center-preserving isomorphism $v^*C(D)\simeq v^*A$ of full recursive pullbacks. The tower $C(D)$ is contracted by its construction, and $A$ is contracted by hypothesis. The cover-synchronization statement ensures that pulling either tower back along $v$ retains every one of its stages, so these really are uncontracted pullbacks with the same lengths as their respective towers. Apply [lem-trf-log-tower-cover-rigidity], second paragraph, to these two towers over $Y$. It gives a unique ordered center-preserving isomorphism $C(D)\simeq A$ whose pullback is this composite. After the canonical identification of step 3 its pullback is exactly $\alpha$, which proves the asserted descent of the comparison.

source.place: VIII 3.3.8--3.3.11 and proof of 3.3.15, pp.108--110: contracted pullbacks and testing equality after descent; non-surjective compatibility expanded.

proof.text: For testing identity and composition, first keep the uncontracted stage labels. Under two consecutive strict etale pullbacks, the ideal generated by the image of the ideal generated by $J_i$ is simply the ideal generated by the composite image of $J_i$; this follows by writing a generator as the image of an element of $J_i$ times an element of the intermediate monoid. A whole ideal remains whole under every pullback [lem-trf-log-tower-cover-synchronization]. Hence deleting it before the next pullback or afterwards gives the same retained original labels. If a retained ideal becomes whole at the second pullback, it is deleted then on both routes. Each count is the number of the surviving original labels below that position; composing the two count maps counts exactly that subset. After a surjective cover, whole-ideal detection at each original level reflects these subsets and therefore reflects equality of count maps and retained embeddings. This uses the induced level covers from step 1; it never assumes that a non-surjective strict etale map reflects properness.

source.place: VIII 3.3.8--3.3.11 and proof of 3.3.15, pp.108--110: contracted pullbacks and testing equality after descent; non-surjective compatibility expanded.

proof.text: Finally the log maps, as well as their index maps, obey these tests. Fix a map of bases and a retained-label choice as in step 5. At the initial level the map is specified. Inductively a map from the next source level to a target blowup is a factorization over the preceding target level, and, whenever it exists, is unique by [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]; when the target stage is deleted this is just the prescribed identity factorization. Thus two recursive comparison maps with the same base map and labels agree on their actual log morphisms, including the maps on log sections. Existence of the two routes being compared follows from their given comparisons and pullback universal properties; their equality follows from this uniqueness. For the intervening tower isomorphisms the cover-reflection and cocycle assertion of [lem-trf-log-tower-cover-rigidity] applies, so the local identity or composition equality descends. Step 5 supplies the common labels and the cover tests, and this argument supplies equality of the maps, not just of the levels. For length zero the induction has only its specified base map, the retained subset is empty, and all the same conclusions follow.
